opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst. She requested admin to Payroll, but admin is reserved for the Payroll Specialist role owner. As a full-time employee, max is write; recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E002 is a contractor with basic security training (note: differs from HR's full_time listing). Contractors max out at read without advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. HR lists E002 as full-time Analyst (max write for Payroll, since Analyst does not own Payroll). However, the Security agent reports the Security DB shows E002 is a contractor with basic security training, for whom access maxes out at read and admin is never allowed. Given the conflicting employment data, I apply the more restrictive, verified interpretation: contractor with basic training → maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds that maximum, so I grant read.

- Security agent: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Comment: contractor max read without advanced training; admin never allowed.

Access policy:
1. full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist owns it). So max for Erika if full_time = write. Requested admin > write, so grant write.
2. contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security says contractor with basic training, so max = read. Requested admin > read, so grant read.

The conflict matters: full_time gives write, contractor basic gives read.
